questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Always use your headlight when riding.
Ride very close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your headlight when riding.
questions.explanation: To be more visible at an intersection, ride with your headlight on. Choose a lane position that gives oncoming traffic a clear view of your motorcycle. Keep enough space between you and other vehicles so you can take quick action if needed. Eye contact alone is not enough to make sure drivers see you.

questions.question: If road conditions require more stopping distance than usual, you should:

options.text: Ask someone else to operate your motorcycle.

questions.explanation: You need more distance between you and the vehicle ahead if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. This is especially important on slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or when traffic is heavy. Use at least a three-second gap.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible across it.

questions.question: When another vehicle is following you too closely, you should:

options.text: Let the other driver pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other driver pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make things more dangerous by encouraging them to tailgate you at higher speed.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the rear brake firmly, then gradually press the front brake.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up out of the wobble.
Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble as this will make your motorcycle less stable. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble. Slowly release the throttle to slow down. Lean your weight as far forward and down as possible. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield should have all of these qualities except:
questions.explanation: Good eye protection and face shields must be free of scratches, resist penetration, give a clear side view, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and fit over eyeglasses or sunglasses. They should not be airtight.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to operate any motorcycle while intoxicated.

questions.question: To reduce your risk of a crash, you should:

options.text: Not use turn signals when changing lanes.
Watch about five feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others by using your turn signals, brake light, and proper lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you. Be prepared to avoid any unexpected hazard.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, you should:

options.text: Hold the handgrips loosely so they can move.
Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
Use a lot of throttle to get over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet because it might come loose and cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
questions.explanation: When riding over rough surfaces, grip the handgrips firmly. This helps you keep control of your motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals are important when riding in groups. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: After entering a turn, you should roll on the throttle and:

options.text: Keep your speed steady or speed up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your speed steady or speed up slowly.
questions.explanation: Roll on the throttle through a turn to stabilize your motorcycle. Keep your speed steady or increase it slowly.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders who wear helmets.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders who wear helmets.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
Move to the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle may weave over rain grooves or bridge gratings, but this is not dangerous. Relax and go straight at a steady speed. Do not weave side to side—this makes the situation worse.

questions.question: Drivers on an entrance ramp may not see you. What should you do to help them merge safely?

options.text: Stay in your lane—it is not your responsibility to be seen.
Move to a lane away from the entrance ramp, if you can.
Weave within your lane to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a lane away from the entrance ramp, if you can.
questions.explanation: Give merging cars plenty of space. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if possible. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to create space for them.

questions.question: When riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway, the best group formation is:
questions.explanation: In curves, turns, and when entering or leaving a highway, riders should switch to a single-file line. Staggered formation is better on straightaways.

questions.question: A passenger should never:
questions.explanation: All passengers should wear helmets and lean with the operator during turns. Passengers should avoid loose clothing that could catch on the motorcycle. Passengers must never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: One sign that your rear tire is flat while riding is:

options.text: A hissing sound from the rear of the bike.
The back end jerks side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. Riders rarely hear a tire failure.

questions.question: The front brake provides how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the rear of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This allows the more experienced riders behind them to watch and help them.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator slow down?
questions.explanation: Downshifting is a way to slow down. Remember that downshifting does not turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: When does alcohol impair your riding ability?

options.text: At about half the legal limit.

questions.explanation: Even one drink can hurt your riding ability. You can be impaired before reaching the legal limit. Never drink alcohol before riding.

questions.question: What should you do when braking on a slippery surface?

options.text: Do not use any brakes; downshift instead.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes when you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: How can you increase your visibility to other drivers?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Also wear bright and reflective clothing, and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: Which provides the best face protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only the eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo, what happens to acceleration and stopping?
questions.explanation: Extra weight from passengers or cargo makes your motorcycle slower to accelerate and slower to stop.

questions.question: What is dangerous about riding alongside another vehicle?

options.text: You can be in the driver's blind spot.
It is safer than riding behind the vehicle.
It is safe because it limits your escape routes.
It should only be done during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another vehicle. The driver may not see you and could move into your lane. Also, you have no escape route if the vehicle blocks you.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT part of a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Check the tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn before every ride. Do a complete inspection before you ride.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever located?
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is located on the left handgrip of the motorcycle.
